artifact.rebuildReason: The CR-02/CR-03/CR-04 correction delta changed application code, which changes the image digest.
artifact.expiryRule: PH-SEC-VEX-POLICY: a NOT_AFFECTED disposition expires at a new image digest. Every disposition below therefore returns to UNDER_INVESTIGATION on this digest until re-approved.

objectiveEquivalence.method: Per PH-SEC-VEX-POLICY, every prior NOT_AFFECTED disposition expires on a new image digest. For each prior row the following axes were compared between the artifact the disposition was produced on and the FINAL artifact: component/package, exact version, architecture, installed files, runtime assumptions, and the assumptions the prior proof itself rested on. Where every axis is identical, the prior analysis is preserved by reference and backed by the objective equivalence evidence. Where any axis changed, the affected analysis is redone — no such axis changed in this delta.

axes.method: Same scanner, same unfiltered command, both artifacts compared row by row on the package purl.
axes.result: identical for all 80 rows (0 added, 0 changed, 0 removed)

axes.method: Debian side: dpkg-query inventory of the FINAL image diffed against the WO-007 artifact inventory. npm side: version carried in the package purl and compared directly.
axes.result: Debian inventory byte-identical (88 packages, zero differences vs the WO-007 artifact). Every npm purl version identical.

axes.method: dpkg architecture field, container uname -m, ELF EI_CLASS/e_machine of the named binaries, and perl Config archname.
axes.result: amd64 / x86_64 unchanged; perl-base amd64; all prior ELF64 assumptions hold.

axes.method: SHA-256 recomputed inside the FINAL image for the exact native artifacts the libstdc++ and libvips proofs named.
axes.result: node, libstdc++.so.6.0.30, sharp-linux-x64-0.35.5.node and libvips-cpp.so.8.18.7 all hash-identical to the WO-008 baseline.

axes.method: Container user, capabilities, privileged flag, published ports, compose commands, live process table and source-level subprocess call sites.
axes.result: Unchanged: uid 1000 (node), not privileged, no cap add/drop, web published on 127.0.0.1:3000 only, worker unpublished, no perl process in either container, no child_process/exec/spawn call site anywhere in apps/ or packages/.

axes.method: Each prior disposition's own evidence claim was re-read and its stated precondition re-measured on the FINAL artifact.
axes.result: Every precondition still holds verbatim; no assumption required re-derivation. Details per row in receipt 08.

Only perl-base 5.36.0-7+deb12u3 is installed, and Archive::Tar is not part of perl-base. Receipt 04.

findings.component: Perl interpreter < 5.40.5-RC1, heap buffer overflow in Perl_study_chunk

revalidation.verdict: NEW_ROW — analysis performed on the FINAL artifact
revalidation.evidence: The vulnerable code IS PRESENT. Perl_study_chunk is the regular-expression compilation path inside the perl interpreter itself; it ships as part of perl-base 5.36.0-7+deb12u3, which is installed on the FINAL artifact, and it is exercised whenever Perl compiles a pattern. This row records that fact rather than hiding it behind a "not present" claim. What the attacker cannot do is drive that code into its vulnerable overflow condition, because the advisory scopes the defect to 32-BIT (ILP32) Perl builds and the FINAL artifact is not one. Measured directly on sha256:eddda17a805b36468dec362df328778cfb285681c9252e4f5e88480064b1cb7c: the installed perl-base is 5.36.0-7+deb12u3 with dpkg architecture amd64; the container kernel is x86_64; the perl binary's ELF header has EI_CLASS=0x02 (ELF64) and e_machine=0x3e (x86-64), so a 32-bit build of this interpreter cannot even be loaded; and the interpreter reports Config{ivsize}=8 bytes (64-bit integer values), Config{longsize}=8 (LONG_BIT=64), Config{ptrsize}=8 (64-bit pointers), ivtype=long, use64bitint=define. The overflow described by the advisory requires the 32-bit integer-width arithmetic that none of these measurements admits, therefore no attacker-controlled input can reach the vulnerable condition on this artifact. Receipt 05. Note explicitly: "Perl is never executed in this container" is NOT part of this justification — it is recorded in receipt 06 only as secondary defence-in-depth and is not what this disposition rests on.
